Nowhttps : **36;2418;TOOLONG ... Kachoris ! Crunchy , flaky &amp; stuffed with oh-so-delicious peas filling , this matar kachori is one of those absolutely unputdownable dishes even the staunchest health freaks among us wo n't be able to turn away from . And for those of you wondering , how many hours will this recipe require you to toll inside the kitchen , let us assure that Mansi Desai from **25;2456;TOOLONG has the perfect shortcut . So , do n't miss it ! <p> Ingredients : <p> 3 cups wheat flour <p> 2 cups of frozen peas <p> 1 ? TBSP Ginger-Chilli paste <p> 1 TSP Garam Masala <p> ? TSP Turmeric Powder <p> 1 TSP Coriander - Cumin Powder <p> 1 TSP Sugar <p> Salt to taste <p> Juice of 1 lemon <p> Oil <p> Method : <p> 1 ) To knead the dough , take some atta or whole wheat flour in a mixing bowl . Add salt as required , water &amp; oil . Knead to a smooth dough . Leave aside for a while 2 ) To prepare the mixture , add peas to a grinder &amp; grind to a coarse mix . We have used frozen peas here . Make sure that the mix is n't too mushy 3 ) In a pan add some oil , followed by the cumin seeds . Once the cumin splutters , add the ginger-chilli paste . Mix around till the raw smell goes away 4 ) Add the peas mix &amp; stir . Add the masalas one after another - turmeric powder , coriander-cumin powder , garam masala , sugar &amp; salt . Add the lemon juice &amp; give it a good mix 5 ) Let the mix cool down . In the meantime , start rolling the kachoris 6 ) Pinch out a portion of the dough &amp; start rolling out . You may use ghee or oil to dip the dough balls 7 ) Spoon in the mix &amp; start closing in from the edges till it resembles a pouch 8 ) Heat oil in a pan &amp; start frying . Once the kachoris are nice &amp; brown on both sides , time to remove them from heat &amp; serve ! <p> #MatarKachori #TheFoodie <p> **37;2483;TOOLONG : //www ... has now entered in the Hathras horror case , former Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh Akhilesh Yadav lashed out Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath . Do watch the video &amp; follow @timesnowfoodie for more such healthy recipes ! <p> METHOD : 1 ) In a mixing bowl , take 1/4 cup Curd and beat it well . 2 ) Into this add 1/4 cup oil &amp; beat it again . 3 ) Now add 3/4 cup melted jaggery ( syrup ) , 3/4 cup Ragi flour , 1/4 cup wheat flour , 1/2 Teaspoon Baking soda &amp; 1 Teaspoon Baking powder . 4 ) Mix it using a cut &amp; fold method . 5 ) Take a kadhai or a pan with lid and preheat it for 10 minutes . 6 ) Now pour this batter in a cake container that is dusted with ragi flour . 7 ) Now allow it to bake in this kadai for 40 -45 minutes . Close the lid . 8 ) Once it is baked , keep it aside . 9 ) Now for the cream , in a pan add 1/2 cup milk . Add 1/2 cup sugar and 2 tablespoon wheat flour . Mix it well and cook it till it thickens 10 ) As it becomes thick like this , keep it aside to cool down . 11 ) Now take 100 gram room temperature Butter and beat it for 1 minute . Keep it in the fridge for 10 minutes . 12 ) When butter becomes hard , beat it again slowly . Beat it till it acquires a creamy consistency . 13 ) Now , add 1-2 Teaspoons of thick mixture that we had made before and beat it really well for some time . 14 ) Now transfer this cream to a piping bag . 15 ) Now decorate this as you wish ! Labour Codes Decoded <p> While the political fire of the Agricultural reforms that the Government brought in has hardly been doused , the Centre has moved swiftly to get three crucial labour reform codes cleared by Parliament in the Monsoon Session . <p> The 3 bills include the Code on Industrial Relations , the Social Security Code and the Code on Occupational Safety , Health and Working Conditions . Already the Government got the Wage Bill cleared by Parliament and notified last year . Together they consolidate the 44 labour laws into 4 different Codes . <p> So what do the three new Codes bring to the table for Employers and Employees ? For one , it will be easier for employers to hire and fire employees . A single licence to hire contract workers will ease doing business in India . But workers will not be able to go on Strike as easily . A 60-day Notice is mandated under the new Code . Also , importantly , the Code empowers the State to adapt labour reforms as per their requirements . <p> Coming at a time when India is facing historic highs on the unemployment front , the jury is still out on whether the new labour laws will make them less rigid for industry to follow and how much they will strengthen the safety net of workers . <p> Catch ET NOW 's Vikram Oza decode the 3 new labour codes . <p> **37;56688;TOOLONG : //www ... Parliament yesterday cleared a Banking Regulation Bill that brings 1,482 urban and 58 multi-state cooperative banks under the country 's Central Bank 's supervision . The idea behind doing so per the Finance Minister , is to bring these cooperative banks under the RBI 's supervision to protect the interests of the depositors and avoid a PMC Bank like crisis in the future . Back in June , when the cabinet had first cleared the bill , Union Minister Prakash Javadekar had stated that this bill will give an assurance to more than 8.6 crore depositors in these banks that their money which amounts to almost 5lk cr , is safe . So what does this move mean for you , if you are one of the 8.6 crore depositors of cooperative bank <p> 1 . Allows the RBI to restructure the stressed cooperative bank without imposing a moratorium on the withdrawal of deposits . Remember last year when the PMC Bank crisis broke out , depositors were able to withdraw a very limited amount from the bank . But now the RBI has the power to manage the crisis via restructuring the bank without necessarily imposing any such restrictions on depositors withdrawal <p> 2 . The RBI will better scrutinise the affairs of the cooperative banks thus keeping a track of their lending , fund raising , deposit accepting activity . This would hel in ensuring no future PMC Bank like issues wherein a large sum of money was lent to the HDIL group . <p> 3 . The RBI may supersede the board of directors in a multi-state cooperative bank for upto 5 years if it feels it is in the interest of the depositors <p> 4 . The cooperative bank is now allowed to lend on the security of its own shares <p> 5 . The cooperative bank is free to open a new place of business of change the location of the bank without requiring RBI permission , thus being able to serve the customer better . <p> **37;57460;TOOLONG : //www ... Bhatia , ET Now : The monsoon session is on and the government is passing critical bills . We decided to do a short primer for our viewers on how bills are passed in the parliament . It all begins with a ministry drafting a text of the proposed law , which is called a ' Bill ' . The ministry seeks views or comments from other ministries , stakeholders and the public . The draft may even be vetted by the Law Ministry and is then presented to the Cabinet for approval . Once the cabinet okays a Bill , it is introduced in Parliament . In Parliament , it goes through three Readings or stages in both Houses . <p> During the First Reading , the Bill is introduced . The introduction of a Bill may be opposed and the matter may be put to a vote in the House . After the introduction , the Bill may be referred to a Standing Committee for examination . The parliamentary panel will consider the broad countors , objectives and will submit its recommendations to the Parliament . The government may or may not accept the Committee 's recommendations . <p> In the Second Reading ( Consideration ) , the Bill is scrutinized . Each clause of the Bill is discussed and may be accepted , amended or rejected . The government , or any MP , may introduce amendments to the Bill at this stage . <p> The final stage is when the bill is ready for passage . The House votes on the redrafted bill . Once the bill is passed in Lok Sabha , it goes through the Rajya Sabha where it will be up for consideration and passage . <p> After both Houses of Parliament pass a Bill , it is presented to the President for assent . After the President gives assent or signs , the Bill is notified as an Act . <p> **37;73930;TOOLONG : //www ... Nowhttps : **36;80150;TOOLONG ... are 3 bills relating to reform in farm sector that 's currently in parliament . All three bills have been passed by lok Sabiha . First one pertains to the agri market , second to contract farming and third relates to essential commodities . These bills are primarily aimed at a ) removing existing barriers that prevents farmers from getting competitive prices <p> and b ) change the system that thwarts the process of legitimate market forces from coming into play due to regulations that have been mired in unfair practices . <p> The farmers and traders will now enjoy the freedom to sell and purchase farm produce outside the registered mandis , which gives them multiple options as opposed to a single mandi system from where the government procures their product . This therefore disempowers the middlemen and the intermediaries that exist between farmers and consumers and takes them directly to the doorstep of the big private players who can offer them higher prices for their produce . <p> The bills seek to open out inter state and intra state trade of farmer produce therefore changing the dynamics of market economics in farmers favour . There is also the facilitatative framework for electronic trading in the current bills which bring in the much needed modernisation and digitization process and upgrades the current trading system . <p> The biggest change is that it allows farmers to directly come into a contract with agri-business firms , exporters , large retailers , removing the tyranny of the middlemen and reducing the cost of marketing by eliminating the ' dalals ' and the power brokers . <p> Besides once the stockholding limits are done away with for certain crops ( cereals , pulses , oilseeds , onions , potatoes ) which earlier came under essential commodities , private sector will trade in these commodities . There would be investment in cold storage and modernizing of food supply chains which will minimize wastage of farm produce . Clearly at this stage some states are vehemently opposing the provisions because they will lose revenue that come in as APMC ( agriculture produce market corporation ) tax . However one can not lose sight of the fact that eliminating ' mandi fees ' will only put more money in the hands of the farmer . <p> Many believe that the provisions work against farmer interests as it will threaten the existing MSP - minimum support price , procurement system since private players may initially offer attractive prices over the mandis but once the mandis become redundant which looks inevitable , they will monopolise the markets and the farmers will then be at the mercy of private entities with little or no regulation . <p> The contention here is that farmers being the weaker section , need regulation and protection which APMC markets even with all its lacunae , were able to provide . Instead of strengthening the existing regulation the farmers are being flung into an open market for which they do not have the wherewithal to compete and survive . Indian farmers can not be subjected to systems that operate in the West because 86 percent of Indian farmers are small and marginal farmers with less than 5 hectares of land . So when it comes to business contracts for instance , private players will be able to exploit them easily . Also the concept of aggregation that the government is proposing for small farmers may not be feasible since ' sponsors ' may not like to deal with a multitude of small farmers . That would again leave bulk of farmers out of the game . In case of dispute resolution also , big private players will have the upper hand and poor farmers will not have the same resources to negotiate with powerful industry lobbies . In fact on the issue of stock holding , if big companies get the license to stock commodities they will inevitably dictate terms to farmers and workout pricing stategy for large scale profiteering without farmers getting any benefit of it . <p> Under the circumstances tighter government regulation can be the only safety net for the farmers which seems to be missing in the current bills . Infact de-licensing and de-regulation is the basic idea of this reform . Ultimately the taste of the pudding is in the eating so unless this model is set in motion there can not be a conclusive argument on whether it 's working in the farmers favour . <p> #TwoSidesWithAfrida <p> **37;80188;TOOLONG : //www ... Nowhttps : **36;104518;TOOLONG ... the name ' multi cap fund ' suggests that the fund invests in an array of stocks from across market capitalisation . In other words , they are market capitalization agnostic . The fund manager can leverage investment opportunities across the spectrum of the market without worrying about a stock 's size and whether it would fit the MF category . For example , large cap funds can invest only in large cap stocks . However , perhaps as an investment strategy , today most of the multi cap funds in existence have a focus on large cap stocks . Large cap stocks form a big majority of the fund 's composition . This could be an approach adopted intentionally by the fund manager in order to reduce the volatility that mid cap and small cap stocks bring about . In order to stay true to its label , SEBI brought about a rule that requires multi cap funds to invest equally across large , mid and small cap stocks . This may enforce the fund manager to buy more mid cap and small cap stocks in his/her portfolio , even if they are unable to find opportunities . While this new avatar of multi cap funds could still be a great way to create wealth , it will entail more risk. **37;104556;TOOLONG : ... Nowhttps : **36;104595;TOOLONG ... As Mahalaya is being celebrated currently which will be followed by Durga Puja , it is a perfect time to learn and make the traditional Bengali rice dish which is prepared during festivals and special occasions . It is ideally made using Gobindobhog rice which is a type of small grain rice but can also be made using the regular Basmati rice . Definitely try this delicious and uniquely flavoured pulao and have it with chhanar dalna , alur dom or a curry of your choice . <p> 1 ) Take 1 cup of washed rice , soak it in water for 30 minutes and drain the water . Marinate the rice with turmeric powder , salt , garam masala and 1 tbsp of ghee.Keep aside for half an hour . <p> 2 ) In a kadai , heat 1 tbsp of ghee . Add 2-3 bay leaves , cumin seeds , cinamon sticks , cashew buts and raisins and stir fry them for 10-15 seconds until the cashews become slightly brown and the raisins swell up . <p> 3 ) Add the marinated rice to the kadai and mix it thoroughly . Make sure that the rice grains do not break , Add 2 tbsp of sugar and a few saffron strands . <p> 4 ) Add 2 cups of water . The ratio of water and rice should be 1:2. 1 cup of rice= 2 cups of water . <p> 5 ) Let it cook on high flame for 10 mins . <p> 6 ) Once the water dries up , cover the kadai with a lid and cook for another 10 mins . <p> 7 ) Turn off flame and rest for 2-3 minutes Basanti Pulav ready to be enjoyed . <p> #BasantiPulao #Mahalaya #TheFoodie <p> **37;121170;TOOLONG : //www ... the first day of the parliament 's monsoon session , the government has made a startling claim . The Securities &amp; Exchange Board Of India issued a clarification circular late last evening standing by their suggested modifications to multi-cap funds . The regulator modified the multi-cap category stating that mutual funds could allocate 75 per cent of total assets to equity &amp; equity related instruments with a minimum of 25 per cent in each large , small &amp; midcap category . Earlier the multi-cap funds had flexibility in terms of allocation towards the various market capitalization categories but it was observed that some multicap funds had skewed portfolios and hence a review of the category was done . Multicap funds should essentially have representation from large , small &amp; midcap category said Swarup Mohanty , CEO , Mirae Asset Global Investments India . The clarification circular also pointed out that the objective was to achieve true to label and appropriate benchmarking . The mutual funds have time till January 2021 to comply with the new norms which is adequate time as per the regulator . It also pointed out the options available to both the mutual funds and unitholders . Some of the available options listed were -- rebalancing the portfolio , switching unitholders to another scheme , merging the multi-cap fund into large &amp; midcap fund . Nowhttps : **36;126779;TOOLONG ... Jan 2021 , your multicap funds will see a rejig in their portfolio . As per the new SEBI rule , multi cap funds are to equally distribute 75% of their total portfolio between large cap , midcap and small cap funds . Currently while the rule is to invest 65% of the fund in equities , most multicap funds today have a good portion of their portfolio in large caps . SEBI 's circular said , " In order to diversify the underlying investments of Multi cap funds across the large , mid and small cap companies and be true to label , it has been decided to partially modify the scheme characteristics of Multi cap fund " <p> Large cap stocks do generally tend to be more stable , less volatile while midcaps and small caps move with more ferocity . With the new SEBI circular , Mutual funds will have to ensure that multi cap funds trim down their large cap stocks to 25% of the total find size while hiking up or buying small cap and mid cap stocks to 25% . Consequently , this may result in wider fluctuations for the multi cap fund NAVs too . <p> For those investors who want equal exposure across all the market caps , this fund would serve that purpose well now . However , the Mutual fund industry may consider changing the category of the fund instead of making the aforementioned rejigs , especially post the recent SEBI clarification that allows the fund houses to convert their multi cap scheme to another scheme category , for instance large cum mid cap scheme . If MFs however , do n't do so , for investor who want to stick to funds with a majority of large cap stocks , it may be time to redeem . <p> **37;126817;TOOLONG : //www ... Nowhttps : **36;145996;TOOLONG ... Bhajiya and Homemade Tomato Sauce ! As monsoon season is about to end in India , why not give it a delicious good-bye with an evening of crunchy ' Prawns Bhajiya ' ? Not only that , why not make a perfect accompaniment for it ; the tomato sauce at home ... yes at home ! and make the evening more blissful ? Here in ' Foodie Jodi ' we have this very combination for you ! Make it , enjoy it and thank us later ! Happy Snacking ! <p> METHOD : 1 . Take 3-4 fresh tomatoes , cut them into 4 big pieces each . Add 1 full glass of water and pressure cook it for 3-4 whistles . Let it boil completely 2 . After 3-4 whistles , switch off the flame and let the tomatoes cool down . After they cool down , transfer the tomato pieces to a blending jar . 3 . Do not discard the tomato stock from the pressure cooker . Transfer it to a cup . 4 . Blend the tomatoes until they form a puree. 5 . Take a big bowl , place a strainer on top of it , add the puree to it in batches and mix it with a spoon to separate the seeds from the puree. 6 . Add the next batch of puree and repeat the same process . Use the leftover tomato stock to extract as much juice as possible . 7 . Heat a pan , add the puree to it and let it stay on flame for 3-4 mins . 8 . Once the puree comes to boil , add 4 tsp of sugar , 1 tsp of salt , 2 tbsp tamarind juice , 1 tsp of kashmiri red chilli powder and combine it well . 9 . Add 1 tsp of white vinegar and combine . Let this boil for 7-8 mins of low medium flame . 10 . After 7-8 mins you will notice that it has reduced . Your tomato sauce is ready ! <p> #PrawnsBhajia #TomatoSauce #TheFoodie <p> **37;146034;TOOLONG : //www ... Bell : Nifty posts best day since 4 Aug led by Reliance . In a bowl , add 1 cup of wheat flour , 2 tbsp refined flour , 1/2 tsp baking powder , a pinch of baking soda , a pinch of salt and give it a quick mix . 2 . The finance ministry is conveniently shifting responsibility to banks when it comes to addressing the issue of waiver , saying any waiver has to be customized and made on a case to case basis otherwise it can be misused and willful defaulters will benefit . Thereby shirking off its own responsibility to bring succour to the woes of the common man reeling under a tremendous crunch to even to meet their basic monthly bills . <p> The NDMA - national disaster management act , in fact , has provisions that government can invoke to create a corpus for dealing with this specific loan repayment crisis which the government is so far unwilling to do . <p> However one must also acknowledge that it can not be a one-sided story . If the borrower is a citizen , the depositor is a citizen too and the government is mandated to protect both . One can not be protected at the cost of the other . Besides , let alone the interest waiver , even the deferred and staggered payments would prove costly for the banks yet on compassionate grounds it 's being considered due to the pandemic crisis . The interest waiver can not be a one size fits all solution . Only those genuinely in need of a bail-out must be identified otherwise it will be a waste of public funds if undeserving candidates are covered under such benefits . After all the banking institutions are also working in public service and government is equally responsible to protect them . Interest waiver will disbalance the entire banking system and that will be counter-productive for a far greater number of people . The banks can always help with restructuring the repayment process for cushioning the repayment deadlines with a more staggered approach . NOW EXPLAINER : DOLLAR CARRY TRADE <p> The dollar carry trade refers to a set of foreign-exchange transactions that seem to exploit an economic anomaly and entail substantial risk . International investors borrow dollars at very low interest rates and invest the funds in a higher yielding , foreign-currency asset . <p> Instead , investors bet that the dollar will continue to depreciate , or at least not appreciate to such an extent as to wipe out their gains on the interest differential . <p> The underlying arbitrage should quickly eliminate the international return differentials by narrowing interest-rate spreads and encouraging the foreign currencies to appreciate in the spot market , and depreciate in the forward market , relative to the dollar . <p> The currencies of countries with low interest rates tend to depreciate , or to not appreciate sufficiently to offset arbitrage opportunities . Persistently low U.S. interest rates and dollar depreciation are consistent with an ongoing carry trade . <p> Indigo aviation makes a dash of 3% . Berger Paints and Bosch both holding out well too . Nowhttps : **36;211046;TOOLONG ... pandemic has hurt the world economy and India 's GDP was not spared either . India 's economy saw a contraction of nearly 24% in the April-June quarter ( Q1FY21 ) on account of the pandemic and this was the worse contraction when compared to some of the advanced economies and BRIC nations . <p> GDP is the gross domestic product and it is a standard indicator used across the globe to measure the health of an economy . GDP represents the monetary value of all goods and services produced by a nation within its borders in a particular period of time . India 's Central Statistic Office ( CSO ) calculates the nation 's GDP . GDP is calculated via two methods , one is economic activity at factor cost and the second is expenditure method at current or market prices . Under the factor cost , method economic activity is measured via 3 main sectors viz Agriculture , Industry , and services which are further divided into 8 sub-sectors . Under the Expenditure method economic activity is measured via spending on trade , private consumption , and investment . Private consumption is denoted by private final consumption expenditure and investment activity is denoted by gross fixed capital formation . <p> While the Indian economy was struggling even before the pandemic , COVID-19 has only accentuated the pain and economists now expect India GDP to contract 6% to 11% in FY21 .
